A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same LSAS study. Their text, equations, figures, tables, and appendices support reliable comparison after matching relocated and renumbered material.

before.justification: v5 reports original synthetic experiments and Cattaneo2 causal-effect estimates in Section 4 and Appendix E.

after.justification: v6 retains those original empirical results and adds graph-density experiments and benchmark runtime measurements in Appendix E.

M1.justification: Algorithms 1–2 retain the same Total Conditioning procedure for discovering Markov blankets and the same R1/R2 adjustment-set search. The discussed descendant-filtering workaround is not incorporated into LSAS.

E1.justification: Appendix E.1.2 extends random-graph coverage from average degree 3 to denser graphs with degrees 5, 7, and 9. The specific structures, four Bayesian benchmark networks, and Cattaneo2 task are retained.

E2.justification: The added density comparison reports EHS alongside CEELS and LDP but excludes LV-IDA (v6 Figure 12). Earlier 40-node random-graph results included LV-IDA and omitted EHS (v5 Figure 10(c)); those original comparisons remain.

E3.justification: The added density study uses 40 nodes, 5K samples, and a 200-second early-stopping threshold for EHS. Appendix E.2.3 adds runtime in seconds as an evaluation measure. Previously reported experimental settings remain unchanged.

E4.justification: Appendix E.1.2 adds a sensitivity analysis testing how increasing graph density affects relative error and conditional-independence test counts. Existing analyses across node counts and sample sizes are retained.

E5.justification: Both versions report averaging 100 repetitions of synthetic experiments and show 95% confidence intervals for Cattaneo2 estimates. The added experiments introduce no new uncertainty-reporting practice or changed run-count statement.

E6.justification: Figures 12 and 14 add density-dependent results and measured runtimes. LSAS has the lowest plotted relative error across tested densities, while LDP sometimes requires fewer tests or less runtime. Original result curves and Cattaneo2 numerical findings are retained.

T1.justification: Section 5 and Figure 7 add a counterexample: S = V2 and Z = {V4, V6} satisfy R1 but yield invalid adjustment when the pretreatment assumption fails. Theorems 1–5 and their Appendix D proofs are unchanged.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction contributions, and conclusion retain the same claims of local covariate selection with latent variables, soundness and completeness under the stated assumptions, and improved efficiency.

C2.justification: Beyond v5's general warning about pretreatment violations, v6 explains how selecting treatment descendants can invalidate adjustment. It also explains why identifying descendants first does not provide a complete workaround.

D1.justification: Section 4 replaces v5's statement that code accompanies supplementary materials with a direct LSAS repository hyperlink. Hardware, conditional-independence test thresholds, and conditioning-set limits remain unchanged.

R1.justification: v6 explicitly credits Entner et al. (2013) when introducing R1 and frames complete local descendant discovery with latent variables as an open problem. The bibliography and Appendix A related-work review are unchanged.

P1.justification: Appendix F becomes main-text Section 5, the conclusion is retitled, and Appendix E gains subsections. Limited clarifications include explicitly naming Markov and faithfulness assumptions already documented in v5. Author and funding text also change.

P2.justification: v6 adds Figures 7, 12, and 14 and moves the Markov-blanket illustration from the appendix to main-text Figure 2. Other figures and tables are retained, with renumbering, relocation, and small caption or panel-label corrections.

improvement.justification: v6 makes the applicability boundary clearer through an explicit failure example, adds density and runtime evidence, and provides a direct code link. These improve transparency and empirical support modestly. The 200-second EHS cutoff and incomplete display of runtime baselines limit the added comparisons; core theory and original findings remain unchanged.
